items.question: Is a file with a Feature: line but no scenarios valid?
items.ticket: Valid files return scenarios in order
items.chose: Returns the feature with an empty scenarios array instead of raising an error.
items.instead: Raise a ParseError saying the feature has no scenarios.

items.question: Which line is reported when the file has no Feature: line at all (empty file)?
items.ticket: Invalid files report the line of the error
items.chose: Reports line 1 when the whole file contains no Feature: line.
items.instead: Report the last line of the file, or the first line with content.

items.question: What happens to free text between the Feature: line and the first Background or Scenario?
items.chose: Silently ignores it as a description, and also accepts any non-keyword text in the header.
items.instead: Raise a ParseError for unrecognised lines, or store the description on the feature.

items.question: How are Scenario Outline: and Examples: handled?
items.chose: Throws a ParseError at the Scenario Outline: line saying it is unsupported.
items.instead: Parse it as an ordinary scenario, or expand it with its Examples.

items.question: Are Background: and a second Background: allowed, and where may a Background appear?
items.chose: Allows one Background, only before the first Scenario, and returns it separately from scenarios. A second one or a late one raises an error.
items.instead: Prepend the background steps to each scenario, or allow it anywhere.

items.question: What happens to tags that are not followed by a Scenario:, or that come before Feature:?
items.chose: Raises a ParseError at the offending line, or at the tag line at end of file. Tags on the Feature: line itself are discarded, and tags before Background: raise an error.
items.instead: Ignore dangling tags, or attach tags to the feature or to Background.

items.question: How is an unclosed doc string reported?
items.ticket: Invalid files report the line of the error
items.chose: Reports the line of the opening delimiter, not the end of the file.
items.instead: Report the last line of the file.

items.question: How are doc string contents processed (indentation, closing delimiter, blank lines)?
items.chose: Strips up to the opening delimiter's indentation from each line, keeps blank lines, and closes on any line that starts with """ after trimming. No escape handling.
items.instead: Keep raw lines unstripped, or require the closing delimiter to match the opening indent and exactly """.

items.question: How are table cells split and what do empty cells and escapes produce?
items.chose: Trims each cell, unescapes \|, \\ and \n, keeps empty cells in the middle, and drops a trailing empty segment after the last bar. A row without a closing bar still keeps its last non-empty cell.
items.instead: Keep cells verbatim without unescaping, or reject rows that do not end with a bar.

items.question: Can a step carry both a table and a doc string, and what if one appears without a step?
items.chose: A step may have only one of the two. A table row or doc string with no preceding step, or one that follows the other kind, raises a ParseError.
items.instead: Allow both on one step, or ignore the stray block.

items.question: Do comments and blank lines between a step and its table or doc string end the attachment?
items.chose: Skips blank and comment lines without clearing the open step, so a table can follow a step after blank or comment lines.
items.instead: Treat blank or comment lines as ending the step's attachment, so a later table raises an error.

items.question: What counts as a step line (keyword spacing, case, localisation, empty text)?
items.chose: Accepts only English keywords Given/When/Then/And/But/* followed by a single space and any text, case-sensitive. A bare keyword with no text is an unrecognised line.
items.instead: Allow a bare keyword or other whitespace after it, accept other languages, or be case-insensitive.
